Security risks disappear because private and public cloud resources share one firewall
Hardware investment is maximised so that the hospital owns each GPU used across its activities
Private data preparation can stay on-premises for privacy while heavy training workloads run in the cloud
Hosting costs disappear because the cloud provider pays for the computing hardware used during training

questions.explanation: Hybrid approaches include developing prototypes locally before scaling to the cloud, keeping sensitive components such as private data preparation on-premises, and using cloud resources for compute-intensive tasks. They do not remove costs, guarantee security, or require owning all hardware. Syllabus reference: CT-AI v2.0, section 1.1.6 (p. 18); AI-1.1.6 (K2).

questions.prompt: A team must deploy a speech model to low-power edge devices and has limited ML experience. Which selection factors from the syllabus are MOST relevant when choosing an ML development framework?

options.text: Deployment considerations for resource-constrained environments, user expertise and the level of community support
Whether the framework stores all data on public clouds, avoids GPU support, and requires manual hyperparameter coding
The framework's market share among web designers, its logo, and the deployment date of its first public release
Whether the framework guarantees bias-free models, removes the need for test data, and replaces the ML workflow

questions.explanation: Selection factors include the application area, rapid prototyping needs, configurability, user expertise, deployment considerations for resource-constrained environments, community support and ecosystem maturity. No framework guarantees bias-free models or replaces testing, and the other lists are unrelated or counterproductive. Syllabus reference: CT-AI v2.0, section 1.1.7 (p. 19); AI-1.1.7 (K2).

questions.prompt: Which TWO statements about AI regulations and standards are consistent with the CT-AI syllabus? Select TWO.

options.text: Countries outside the EU have uniformly adopted stricter regulations than the EU
The ISO/IEC 42119 series of standards was withdrawn because the EU AI Act covers testing
AI regulations and standards need regular review to stay relevant as AI evolves
Soft law instruments carry the same financial penalties as the EU AI Act
Sector-specific AI regulations are emerging in areas such as healthcare and finance

questions.explanation: The syllabus notes emerging sector-specific regulation in healthcare and finance and stresses that regulations and standards must be regularly reviewed and updated. The ISO/IEC 42119 series is being developed, many nations outside the EU favour lighter-touch regulation, and soft law has no fines. Syllabus reference: CT-AI v2.0, section 1.1.8 (p. 20); AI-1.1.8 (K2).

questions.prompt: Which statement about AI functional correctness in ISO/IEC 25059 is correct?

options.text: It requires an AI-based system to give the correct expected output in all of its test cases before release
It describes the ability of an operator to intervene in the system to prevent harm or hazard
It considers both correct and incorrect outputs and defines acceptable thresholds for incorrect results
It is a quality-in-use characteristic that measures how satisfied users feel with AI explanations

questions.explanation: Because a certain error rate is expected from probabilistic ML, ISO/IEC 25059 adjusts functional correctness to consider correct and incorrect outputs and acceptable thresholds for incorrect results. It is a product-quality characteristic, not user satisfaction, and intervention to prevent harm is intervenability. Syllabus reference: CT-AI v2.0, section 2.1.1 (p. 22); AI-2.1.1 (K2).

questions.prompt: Which statement about explainable AI techniques such as LIME in safety-related systems is consistent with the syllabus?

options.text: They are mandatory under all mature functional safety standards, which require AI components to be explainable
They make each decision of a deep neural network fully transparent, so regulators accept them as complete proof of safety
They replace testing of AI-based systems, because an explained decision is assumed to be a correct decision
They can provide insight into an AI-based system's reasoning, but they are not widely available and may compromise system performance

questions.explanation: Explainable AI techniques such as LIME can give insights into reasoning, but the syllabus notes they are not widely available and may cost performance. They do not give complete proof, mature functional safety standards do not include AI and some prohibit it, and explanation does not replace testing. Syllabus reference: CT-AI v2.0, section 2.1.2 (p. 23); AI-2.1.2 (K2).

questions.prompt: A chatbot provider defines: 'The chatbot must score at least 95% in an internal red-teaming assessment of refusing content that promotes violence, self-harm or hate speech.' Which characteristic does this acceptance criterion address?

options.text: Functional adaptability (product quality)
AI functional correctness (product quality)
Transparency (interaction capability and satisfaction)
Societal and ethical risk mitigation (quality in use)

questions.explanation: Refusing harmful content addresses societal and ethical risk mitigation, which covers areas such as safety, human values and non-discrimination. Functional correctness would measure task accuracy, adaptability concerns autonomous change, and controllability concerns timely human intervention. Syllabus reference: CT-AI v2.0, section 2.2.1 (p. 24); AI-2.2.1 (K2).

questions.prompt: Which challenges are specific to applying reinforcement learning, according to the CT-AI syllabus?

options.text: Setting up the environment, designing the reward function and selecting the best strategy to meet the goal
Collecting labelled numerical targets, fitting a regression line and scaling the input features
Labelling enough training examples, balancing the classes and choosing the confusion-matrix orientation
Choosing the number of clusters, selecting the distance measure and naming the resulting customer segments

questions.explanation: The syllabus lists setting up the environment, designing the reward function and selecting the best strategy as reinforcement-learning challenges. Labelling and class balance relate to supervised classification, cluster choices to clustering, and numerical targets to ML regression. Syllabus reference: CT-AI v2.0, section 3.1.1 (p. 27); AI-3.1.1 (K2).

questions.prompt: A team fine-tunes a pretrained language model, known to produce biased outputs, using high-quality data for a new support task. What should testers conclude?

options.text: High-quality task data removes biases in the pretrained model, so fairness testing can be skipped for the fine-tuned model
Biases in the pretrained model can carry over, so the new model must be tested to confirm it performs reliably and fairly
Biases arise from RAG retrieval rather than model weights, so a fine-tuned model needs no fairness testing
Fine-tuning resets all weights of the pretrained model, so earlier biases are irrelevant to the fine-tuned model

questions.explanation: The syllabus warns that biases or vulnerabilities in a pretrained model typically carry over to the new model, so testing is necessary to confirm reliable and fair behavior. Good data does not guarantee removal of bias, fine-tuning builds on existing weights, and bias is not limited to RAG. Syllabus reference: CT-AI v2.0, section 3.1.4 (p. 30); AI-3.1.4 (K2).

questions.prompt: Which statement about data preparation is consistent with the CT-AI syllabus?

options.text: It is typically an iterative, often manual process in which activities may be reordered or omitted for a given project
It must follow a fixed order of acquisition, cleaning and labelling, whatever the project requirements are
It is fully automated by ML frameworks, so testers need to check the trained model rather than the data
It uses less effort than model selection and building, because modern algorithms tolerate poor-quality data

questions.explanation: The syllabus describes data preparation as iterative and often manual, with activities reordered or omitted based on project needs; it is one of the most resource-intensive workflow activities. Framework support does not remove the need to test the data, and poor data quality undermines models. Syllabus reference: CT-AI v2.0, section 3.2.1 (p. 31); AI-3.2.1 (K2).

questions.prompt: A team with very little data uses cross-validation but keeps no hold-out test set. How should the averaged cross-validation performance be interpreted?

options.text: It is optimistically biased and cannot serve as an unbiased estimate of how well the model generalises
It is equivalent to a hold-out test result because the folds were stratified by class
It is pessimistically biased because averaging across folds reduces the reported accuracy
It is an unbiased estimate because each record was used for validation exactly once

questions.explanation: The syllabus states that when a hold-out test set is not feasible, the average cross-validation performance is optimistically biased and cannot be an unbiased estimate, because the same data guided tuning. Stratification and fold rotation do not remove that bias. Syllabus reference: CT-AI v2.0, section 3.2.3 (p. 32); AI-3.2.3 (K2).

questions.prompt:
Three candidate models are tested on the same 500 support tickets, 100 of which are urgent. The acceptance criteria require recall of at least 85% and precision of at least 70% for the 'urgent' class.
Model P: TP 90, FP 45, FN 10, TN 355
Model Q: TP 86, FP 30, FN 14, TN 370
Model R: TP 80, FP 10, FN 20, TN 390
Which models meet BOTH criteria?

options.text: Models P and Q
Model P alone
Models Q and R
Model Q alone

questions.explanation: Model P: recall 90.0%, precision 66.7%, so it fails precision. Model Q: recall 86.0%, precision 74.1%, so it meets both. Model R: recall 80.0%, precision 88.9%, so it fails recall despite the highest precision. Syllabus reference: CT-AI v2.0, section 3.3.1 (p. 33); AI-3.3.1 (K3).

questions.prompt: Which statement about the single-layer perceptron is correct?

options.text: It can learn any non-linear decision boundary because it contains several hidden layers of neurons
It cannot be trained with labelled data, so it is used only for unsupervised clustering of incoming email messages
It can learn binary classifiers for linearly separable problems by separating two categories with a straight line
It is the modern standard for image recognition, replacing convolutional neural networks in vision tasks

questions.explanation: The single-layer perceptron, one of the earliest neural networks, supports supervised learning of binary classifiers for linearly separable problems, such as separating spam and non-spam with a straight line. It has one layer, it is not the modern vision standard, and it learns from labelled data. Syllabus reference: CT-AI v2.0, section 3.4.1 (p. 36); AI-3.4.1 (K2).

questions.prompt: Why should testers combine neural-network coverage measures with techniques such as adversarial and metamorphic testing?

options.text: Coverage measures can be calculated after deployment alone, so the network needs other techniques before release
Coverage measures are required by the EU AI Act, so other techniques serve documentation purposes
High structural coverage does not show that the network generalises well, because it can activate neurons for the wrong reasons
Coverage measures replace the need for test data, so other techniques are needed to generate the data

questions.explanation: Structural coverage reveals untested areas, but neural networks can learn spurious correlations and give correct activations for incorrect reasons, so it does not guarantee generalisation. Coverage is measured during testing, needs test inputs, and is not a regulatory documentation requirement in the syllabus. Syllabus reference: CT-AI v2.0, section 3.4.3 (p. 37); AI-3.4.3 (K2).

questions.prompt: An adaptive recommendation system keeps learning from user behavior after deployment. Which testing approach does the syllabus suggest?

options.text: Prepare test cases for every behavior the system could learn in future, so that each adaptation can be verified before it happens
Build an automated suite focused on core functionality, run it after significant changes, and check that performance has not degraded beyond a threshold
Freeze the system during testing and accept the test results as valid for the whole lifetime of the adaptive system in production
Rely on the users to report defects, because the behavior of an adaptive system cannot be tested before or after deployment

questions.explanation: Because new behaviors of an adaptive system cannot always be predicted, an automated suite focused on core functionality can be run whenever the system changes significantly, and testing can check that performance has not degraded beyond a threshold. Future behaviors cannot be enumerated in advance, and test results do not stay valid as the system adapts. Syllabus reference: CT-AI v2.0, section 4.1.1 (p. 39); AI-4.1.1 (K2).

questions.prompt: Which techniques does the CT-AI syllabus mention for quantifying the accuracy, fairness and robustness of AI-based systems under uncertainty and bias?

options.text: Code reviews, pair programming and static analysis
Confidence intervals, hypothesis testing and error analysis
Load testing, soak testing and spike testing
Statement coverage, branch coverage and decision table testing

questions.explanation: Statistical testing lets practitioners quantify and analyse model accuracy, fairness and AI robustness with measures such as confidence intervals, hypothesis testing and error analysis. Structural coverage, reviews and load testing are useful elsewhere but do not address statistical uncertainty in model outputs. Syllabus reference: CT-AI v2.0, section 4.1.2 (p. 40); AI-4.1.2 (K2).

questions.prompt: Users of a virtual assistant disagree about what a good answer to 'plan a relaxing weekend' looks like. Which test oracle difficulty does this illustrate?

options.text: Complexity of tasks
Self-learning systems
Subjectivity of behavior
Incomplete specifications

questions.explanation: The correctness of an AI-based system's behavior can be subjective; expectations for virtual assistants vary widely, which complicates agreeing expected results. Task complexity concerns outputs too complex to verify, self-learning concerns changing behavior, and exploratory development concerns missing specifications. Syllabus reference: CT-AI v2.0, section 4.1.3 (p. 40); AI-4.1.3 (K2).

questions.prompt: Which measures does the syllabus list for non-functional testing of a GenAI system's resource utilisation?

options.text: Neuron coverage, kMNC and neuron boundary coverage of the model
CPU and GPU usage, memory consumption, network bandwidth and response times
Precision, recall, F1-score and accuracy on the training dataset
Originality, novelty, coherence and creativity of generated text

questions.explanation: Non-functional testing of GenAI evaluates resource utilisation during inference and training using measures such as CPU and GPU usage, memory consumption, network bandwidth and response times. Classification metrics, content quality aspects and neural-network coverage measure other things. Syllabus reference: CT-AI v2.0, section 4.2.1 (p. 41); AI-4.2.1 (K2).

questions.prompt: A five-person expert red team has found 40 failures in a GenAI customer-service assistant. Management wants much broader coverage of the attack space before launch. Which approach is MOST appropriate?

options.text: Stop red teaming now and rely on blue-team filters after launch, because live users will reveal the remaining attack space
Restrict testing to single-turn prompts so that the existing five testers can execute many more prompts per hour
Combine the testers with an LLM that generates many attack prompts and another LLM that checks the outputs, reviewing samples manually
Replace the red team with a public benchmark suite, because standardised datasets cover the possible attacks on the customer-service assistant

questions.explanation: To extend coverage beyond small expert teams, organisations use crowd-sourced prompts, automated approaches where an LLM generates attack prompts and another LLM checks outputs, or hybrid approaches combining human creativity with automation. Blue teaming complements but does not replace pre-deployment red teaming, benchmarks are static, and multi-turn dialogues are a core red-teaming activity. Syllabus reference: CT-AI v2.0, section 4.2.2 (p. 42); AI-4.2.2 (K3).

questions.prompt: Which TWO checks belong to component integration testing of a machine learning system? Select TWO.

options.text: Training data is compared with operational data to test its representativeness
End-to-end prediction time is measured on the complete, fully assembled system
Data exchanges with an external partner system are checked in a production-like setup
Predictions from the model are passed to the user interface and used correctly
Inputs from the data pipeline are received by the model in the expected format

questions.explanation: Component integration testing checks that pipeline inputs arrive as the model expects and that predictions are exchanged with and used correctly by other components such as the user interface. Representativeness belongs to input data testing, end-to-end timing to system testing and external exchanges to system integration testing. Syllabus reference: CT-AI v2.0, section 4.3.1 (p. 43); AI-4.3.1 (K2).

questions.prompt: Which statement about risk-based testing of AI-based systems is consistent with the CT-AI syllabus?

options.text: ML risks are project risks alone, because the AI-based system itself cannot be a source of product risks
There is one standard taxonomy of ML risks, defined by the EU AI Act, which every organisation must use without changes
Most regulatory frameworks require a risk-based approach, and risks can be categorised by workflow area or by ISO/IEC 25059 quality characteristics
Risk-based testing applies to conventional systems but is replaced by statistical testing for systems containing AI components

questions.explanation: Risk-based testing should be applied to all systems, most regulatory frameworks require a risk-based approach, and there is no standard way to categorise ML risks; the workflow areas and the ISO/IEC 25059 characteristics are two options. ML risks include both project and product risks. Syllabus reference: CT-AI v2.0, section 4.3.2 (p. 44); AI-4.3.2 (K2).

questions.prompt: A data scientist suspects that the attributes chosen as model inputs do not capture the factors that matter for the prediction. Which mitigation does the syllabus list for this risk?

options.text: Shadow testing
Feature testing
Rollback testing
Back-to-back testing

questions.explanation: Sub-optimal feature selection is mitigated by feature testing in the input data risk table. Back-to-back testing compares system versions, and rollback and shadow testing belong to deployment testing. Syllabus reference: CT-AI v2.0, section 5.1.1 (p. 47); AI-5.1.1 (K2).

questions.prompt: When performing disparate impact analysis, which precaution does the CT-AI syllabus recommend?

options.text: Avoid combinations of sensitive attributes, because hidden bias cannot occur when attributes interact with each other
Confirm that the counterfactual examples are realistic, because the model may react to unrealistic inputs rather than to underlying bias
Change several unrelated attributes in each counterfactual as well, so that the model cannot recognise which sensitive attribute is being tested
Use a single counterfactual per sensitive attribute, so that results are not distorted by multiple statistical tests

questions.explanation: Counterfactuals must not be unrealistic, or the model may respond to them instead of to any underlying bias; the analysis can also cover combinations of sensitive attributes to find hidden bias. Many tests are needed for a statistically significant result, and changing unrelated attributes would confound it. Syllabus reference: CT-AI v2.0, section 5.1.2 (p. 48); AI-5.1.2 (K2).

questions.prompt: How should the test strategy differ between a training data pipeline and an operational data pipeline?

options.text: Training and operational pipelines need identical strategies because they must contain exactly the same code
Training pipeline testing is unnecessary because operational pipelines alone contain defects that affect model predictions
Training pipeline testing may focus on data integrity, while operational pipeline testing prioritises reliability, performance and maintainability
Training pipeline testing prioritises reliability and performance, while operational pipeline testing focuses on exploratory prototypes

questions.explanation: Test strategies must align with the pipeline's purpose: training pipelines, often exploratory prototypes, may focus on data integrity, while operational pipeline testing prioritises reliability, performance and maintainability. Defects in either pipeline affect the model, and their strategies differ. Syllabus reference: CT-AI v2.0, section 5.1.3 (p. 49); AI-5.1.3 (K2).

questions.prompt: Which sources does the syllabus suggest for identifying the expected operational data distributions and critical edge cases?

options.text: Domain experts, data from existing or similar systems, and benchmark datasets from trusted bodies such as NIST
The confusion matrix of the current model, the test team's velocity, and the sprint burndown chart
The model's training loss, the framework's default settings, and the ML engineer's preferred hyperparameter values
The model card of a competitor, the marketing plan, and the number of downloads of the mobile application

questions.explanation: Expected operational distributions and edge cases are identified by consulting domain experts, analysing data from existing or similar systems and using benchmark datasets from trusted sources such as NIST. The other lists do not describe the real-world target population. Syllabus reference: CT-AI v2.0, section 5.1.4 (p. 50); AI-5.1.4 (K2).

questions.prompt: A dataset records the points awarded in each season of a 10-team league. Each team plays every other team once (45 matches); a win gives the winner 3 points and a draw gives each team 1 point. The team defines a constraint that the season's total points must be at least 90 and at most 135. Which statement correctly applies dataset constraint testing?

options.text: It is a range constraint on one value, and a season with 138 total points violates it
It is a sum constraint, and a season with 112 total points violates it
It is a sum constraint, and a season with 138 total points violates it
It is a count constraint, and a season with exactly 90 total points violates it

questions.explanation: The rule limits the sum of values across all match records, so it is a multi-value sum constraint. With 45 matches, the total lies between 45 × 2 = 90 (all draws) and 45 × 3 = 135 (no draws), so 138 is impossible and violates it, while 112 and 90 are valid. It is not a single-value range constraint or a count of non-null values. Syllabus reference: CT-AI v2.0, section 5.1.5 (p. 51); AI-5.1.5 (K3).

questions.prompt: A team has budget to re-check only 5% of 200,000 labelled road images. Which approach to selecting the images does the syllabus recommend?

options.text: Random selection, because any prioritisation introduces bias into the label correctness assessment of the dataset
Selection of the largest image files, because high-resolution images are more likely to contain labelling defects
Risk-based prioritisation, focusing on ambiguous images near class boundaries and images most likely to affect success or safety
Selection of the newest images, because older labels have already been validated by the deployed model's accuracy

questions.explanation: Expert reviews and multiple annotation can be focused using risk-based prioritisation based on the likelihood of mislabelling, such as ambiguous points near class boundaries, and on the data most likely to affect success or safety. The other selection rules are not grounded in mislabelling risk. Syllabus reference: CT-AI v2.0, section 5.1.6 (p. 52); AI-5.1.6 (K2).

questions.prompt: Which mitigations does the model risk table give for a lack of model AI robustness due to unexpected inputs?

options.text: Rollback testing and smoke testing
A/B testing and shadow testing
Requirements review and exploratory testing
Adversarial testing and fuzz testing

questions.explanation: Lack of model AI robustness due to unexpected inputs is mitigated by adversarial testing and fuzz testing. A/B and shadow testing compare versions, rollback and smoke testing address deployment, and requirements review with exploratory testing addresses poor system requirements. Syllabus reference: CT-AI v2.0, section 6.1.1 (p. 55); AI-6.1.1 (K2).

questions.prompt: Why does documentation play a larger role for ML models than for many conventional systems?

options.text: Models are hard to inspect, black-box in nature, dependent on data and updated many times, so documentation becomes the main tool for understanding them
Models are tested by regulators rather than testers, so documentation replaces the test reports that conventional systems need
Models are written in natural language, so documentation is needed to translate them into code that reviewers can inspect directly
Models do not change after release, so documentation written once at deployment remains accurate for the model's whole lifetime

questions.explanation: Machine-generated code has limited understandability, models are black boxes that depend on data and are frequently updated, so documentation becomes the main tool for developers, testers and regulators to understand, evaluate and trust them. Models change frequently, and documentation does not replace testing. Syllabus reference: CT-AI v2.0, section 6.1.2 (p. 56); AI-6.1.2 (K2).

questions.prompt: Why might a team use sequential testing when checking an accuracy target with a statistical criterion?

options.text: It analyses results as they accumulate and lets the team stop early once there is sufficient evidence for or against the goal
It replaces the independent test dataset with the validation dataset so that fewer new test cases need to be created
It removes the need for a margin of error because each test case is evaluated in sequence by a human expert
It runs the test cases in a fixed sequence so that the confidence level remains constant regardless of the results observed so far

questions.explanation: Sequential testing provides a formal statistical framework for early stopping: results are analysed as they accumulate and testing stops when sufficient evidence supports or rejects the accuracy target. It does not fix the confidence level, reuse validation data or remove the margin of error. Syllabus reference: CT-AI v2.0, section 6.1.3 (p. 57); AI-6.1.3 (K2).

questions.prompt: What is the main benefit of identifying vulnerabilities through adversarial testing?

options.text: Developers can remove the data pipeline, because adversarial testing validates the input data during operation
Developers can stop testing the model's accuracy, because robustness to adversarial examples implies high accuracy
Developers can add safeguards that make the model more robust against accidental adversarial examples and malicious adversarial attacks
Developers can replace the training dataset, because adversarial examples are better training data than real inputs

questions.explanation: Identifying vulnerabilities lets developers incorporate safeguards and make the model more robust, both against accidental adversarial examples and against adversarial attacks that use them maliciously. Robustness does not imply accuracy, and adversarial testing does not replace the pipeline or the training data. Syllabus reference: CT-AI v2.0, section 6.1.4 (p. 58); AI-6.1.4 (K2).

questions.prompt:
A risk-assessment model predicts age at death. Source test case: a 45-year-old non-smoker is predicted 82 years. The metamorphic relation states that increasing the number of cigarettes smoked per day, all else unchanged, should decrease the prediction. Follow-up results:
F1: 10 cigarettes per day, prediction 78
F2: 20 cigarettes per day, prediction 80
What should the tester conclude?

options.text: The relation is violated because F1 predicts a lower age than the source, so the source test case must be wrong
The relation is violated because F2, with heavier smoking, predicts a higher age than F1, so a potential defect should be reported
The test is inconclusive because metamorphic testing needs the exact expected age for each follow-up test case
Both follow-ups pass because each prediction is below 82, so the relation holds and no defect needs to be reported

questions.explanation: The monotonicity relation implies that more cigarettes should give a lower prediction, so 20 per day must not predict a higher age than 10 per day; F2 (80) above F1 (78) violates it. Checking each follow-up only against the source misses this, metamorphic testing checks relations rather than exact values, and F1 below 82 is expected. Syllabus reference: CT-AI v2.0, section 6.1.5 (p. 59); AI-6.1.5 (K3).

questions.prompt: A film recommendation service wants to use feedback for dynamic drift testing. Which pairing of direct and indirect feedback is correct?

options.text: Direct: the user rates a recommendation; indirect: data on which films the user actually watched
Direct: the training labels; indirect: the distribution of predicted film genres
Direct: the model's confidence score; indirect: the number of films in the catalogue
Direct: data on which films the user actually watched; indirect: the user's rating of a recommendation

questions.explanation: The syllabus gives a user rating a recommendation as direct feedback and data extracted from the films the user has watched as indirect feedback. Confidence scores, catalogue size, training labels and predicted distributions are not user feedback. Syllabus reference: CT-AI v2.0, section 6.1.7 (p. 60); AI-6.1.7 (K2).

questions.prompt: When should testing for overfitting and underfitting take place?

options.text: During rollback testing of the deployed operational model
During data acquisition, before any labelling
During training, evaluation and tuning of the model
After deployment, as part of canary testing

questions.explanation: The syllabus states that testing for overfitting and underfitting should occur during training, evaluation and tuning, the activities that generate the model. Canary and rollback testing belong to deployment, and data acquisition precedes model training. Syllabus reference: CT-AI v2.0, section 6.1.8 (p. 60); AI-6.1.8 (K2).

questions.prompt: Which statistical techniques does the CT-AI syllabus list as the most popular for A/B testing?

options.text: Precision, recall, accuracy and F1-score
Kolmogorov-Smirnov, ANOVA, bootstrap and k-fold cross-validation
Cohen's Kappa, percentage agreement, Gini index and entropy
t-test, z-test, chi-squared test and Mann-Whitney U test

questions.explanation: The syllabus names the t-test, z-test, chi-squared test and Mann-Whitney U test as the most popular statistical techniques for A/B testing. Kappa measures annotator agreement, Kolmogorov-Smirnov is used for distributions and drift, and confusion-matrix metrics measure classification performance. Syllabus reference: CT-AI v2.0, section 6.1.9 (p. 61); AI-6.1.9 (K2).

questions.prompt: For functional back-to-back testing, which requirement applies to the pseudo-oracle?

options.text: It needs to match the functional behavior of the system under test, but not its non-functional requirements, which can make it cheaper to build
It needs to match both the functional and the non-functional requirements, so it costs as much as the system under test
It needs to be the previous production release, because a newly built pseudo-oracle cannot be trusted as a reference
It needs to use the same ML framework and algorithm as the system under test, so that outputs are directly comparable

questions.explanation: For functional back-to-back testing, the pseudo-oracle only needs to match functional behavior and not the same non-functional requirements, potentially making it less expensive to build. It can be an existing system or one built for testing, and ideally it uses different frameworks or algorithms. Syllabus reference: CT-AI v2.0, section 6.1.10 (p. 62); AI-6.1.10 (K2).

questions.prompt: Which mitigations does the syllabus give for the risk of sub-optimal hyperparameter selection, such as an unsuitable network structure or learning rate?

options.text: Security testing and usability testing
Smoke testing and rollback testing
ML functional performance testing and A/B testing
Data provenance testing and data representativeness testing

questions.explanation: Sub-optimal hyperparameter selection is mitigated by ML functional performance testing and A/B testing. Smoke and rollback testing target deployment, security and usability testing target framework qualities, and provenance and feature testing target input data. Syllabus reference: CT-AI v2.0, section 7.1.1 (p. 64); AI-7.1.1 (K2).

questions.prompt: Which activities belong to installability testing of a machine learning system?

options.text: Comparing the converted model's accuracy, inference speed and memory use with those of the model in its original training format
Releasing the model to 5% of users after installation, monitoring latency, accuracy and error rates in real time before a full rollout
Checking that error messages and inputs and outputs of the model's interfaces comply with standards for external clients
Installing, configuring and uninstalling it across supported environments, including dependencies such as GPU drivers and the installation scripts

questions.explanation: Installability testing verifies that the MLS can be installed, configured and uninstalled across supported environments, including dependencies such as GPU drivers, framework compatibility and installation scripts. The other options describe canary, model conversion and API testing. Syllabus reference: CT-AI v2.0, section 7.1.2 (p. 65); AI-7.1.2 (K2).

questions.prompt: An insurance company compares two claim-triage systems. System X applies 40 documented if-then rules; System Y was trained on 200,000 historical claims. Which statement about System Y is MOST accurate?

options.text: It will give the same result as System X because both systems are based on the same historical claims
It needs no explainability support because insurance is not a domain in which decisions must be justified
It may give unexpected outputs for unusual claims because it generalises from patterns rather than following explicit rules
It can be fully verified by reviewing its code line by line because its decisions map to programmed rules

questions.explanation: System Y is ML-based: it extracts patterns from data, which allows it to handle ambiguity but makes outputs less predictable and harder to explain. Line-by-line review fits System X, the two systems are built differently, and explainability matters in finance and insurance. Syllabus reference: CT-AI v2.0, section 1.1.1 (p. 15); AI-1.1.1 (K2).

questions.prompt: What does the term 'technological singularity' refer to in the CT-AI syllabus?

options.text: The stage in the ML workflow where a deployed model starts learning from operational data
The release of the first frontier model that outperforms human experts on a widely used standard benchmark
The moment a narrow AI system is retrained successfully to perform a second, unrelated task
The point at which AI-based systems would move from general AI to super AI, if that were to occur

questions.explanation: The syllabus calls the transition from general AI to super AI, if it ever happens, the technological singularity. Benchmark success and retraining for a new task describe narrow AI, and learning from operational data describes adaptive systems. Syllabus reference: CT-AI v2.0, section 1.1.2 (p. 15); AI-1.1.2 (K2).

questions.prompt: Which statement about agentic AI is consistent with the CT-AI syllabus?

options.text: It is a type of convolutional neural network that improves image classification accuracy by adding more hidden layers
It is a data preparation activity that automatically labels the training data before any supervised learning starts
It extends AI technologies with autonomous agents that plan, reason and act independently to achieve goals in dynamic environments
It is a hardware architecture that replaces the von Neumann design with brain-inspired neuromorphic processing circuits

questions.explanation: The syllabus describes agentic AI as extending AI technologies through autonomous agents that plan, reason and act toward goals. CNNs are a deep learning technique, neuromorphic processors are the brain-inspired hardware, and labelling belongs to data acquisition. Syllabus reference: CT-AI v2.0, section 1.1.3 (p. 16); AI-1.1.3 (K2).

questions.prompt: Which statement about practical GenAI tools reflects the CT-AI syllabus?

options.text: Most practical GenAI tools avoid multimodal input because combining text and images reduces output quality
Most practical GenAI tools are trained from scratch for each customer because pretrained models cannot be adapted
Most practical GenAI tools rely on GANs for text, because transformers are restricted to image generation
Most practical GenAI tools are based on foundation models that are then fine-tuned for specific applications

questions.explanation: The syllabus states that most practical GenAI tools are based on foundation models fine-tuned for specific applications, and that the field is moving toward multimodal models. Transformers underpin LLMs, and training from scratch for each customer is the costly approach fine-tuning avoids. Syllabus reference: CT-AI v2.0, section 1.1.4 (p. 17); AI-1.1.4 (K2).

questions.prompt: Which statement about hardware for machine learning systems is correct?

options.text: Different hardware may be used for training and inference, such as cloud hardware for training and a phone for running the model
General-purpose CPUs are the best option for small-scale ML work because they have higher clock speeds than any GPU
AI-specific chips such as ASICs are mainly used for cloud training, while GPUs are mainly used at the edge
The same hardware must be used for training and for inference, otherwise the trained weights of the model cannot be loaded at runtime

questions.explanation: The syllabus gives the example of a speech model that runs on a low-end phone but needs cloud computing to train. For small-scale ML work GPUs are generally the best option, and AI-specific chips such as ASICs are best suited for edge computing with training done in the cloud. Syllabus reference: CT-AI v2.0, section 1.1.5 (p. 18); AI-1.1.5 (K2).

questions.prompt: Which factor list BEST reflects what determines the optimal development and hosting solution for an AI model?

options.text: The number of lines of code in the training script, the source control branching model, and the build server's operating system
The programming language of the user interface, the number of testers, and the brand of the test management tool
Model size and complexity, performance needs, budget, security and privacy, deployment needs and regulatory requirements
The colour scheme of the product, the date of the next marketing campaign, and the team's preferred IDE

questions.explanation: The syllabus lists model size, complexity, performance requirements, budget constraints, security and data privacy, deployment needs and regulatory requirements, and notes that development and hosting are usually decided separately. The other lists contain factors unrelated to AI development and hosting. Syllabus reference: CT-AI v2.0, section 1.1.6 (p. 18); AI-1.1.6 (K2).

questions.prompt: Which framework function iteratively adjusts a model's internal parameters, based on example data and the desired result, to improve its performance?

options.text: Deployment to target platforms
Training and optimisation
Data handling and preprocessing
Evaluation on unseen data

questions.explanation: Training and optimisation algorithms iteratively adjust the model's internal parameters based on training data and the desired result, and may support distributed training or fine-tuning. Data handling prepares data, deployment converts models for target platforms, and documentation is not listed as a framework function. Syllabus reference: CT-AI v2.0, section 1.1.7 (p. 19); AI-1.1.7 (K2).

questions.prompt: What is the core aim of AI regulations and standards according to the CT-AI syllabus?

options.text: To slow the adoption of AI until general AI can be safely regulated by one global authority
To remove the need for testing by certifying AI-based systems before their development
To foster trust in AI and help realise its benefits while mitigating potential harms
To standardise ML frameworks so that all organisations use the same development tools

questions.explanation: The syllabus states that the core aim is to foster trust in AI and promote realisation of its benefits while mitigating potential harms, ideally making systems safe, fair, transparent, sustainable, accountable and ethical. Regulation does not mandate one framework, replace testing or wait for general AI. Syllabus reference: CT-AI v2.0, section 1.1.8 (p. 20); AI-1.1.8 (K2).

questions.prompt: ISO/IEC 25059 introduces 'societal and ethical risk mitigation'. Under which characteristic and perspective does it appear?

options.text: As a sub-characteristic of freedom from risk, from the quality-in-use perspective
As a sub-characteristic of interaction capability, from the quality-in-use perspective
As a sub-characteristic of reliability, from the product-quality perspective
As a sub-characteristic of functional suitability, from the product-quality perspective

questions.explanation: Societal and ethical risk mitigation is a quality-in-use sub-characteristic of freedom from risk, covering accountability, fairness, privacy, human control of technology and more. AI robustness falls under reliability, functional adaptability under functional suitability, and user controllability and transparency under interaction capability. Syllabus reference: CT-AI v2.0, section 2.1.1 (p. 22); AI-2.1.1 (K2).

questions.prompt: How does the EU AI Act treat AI systems used as safety components in areas such as aviation, medical devices or automotive?

options.text: It classifies them as minimal risk when they are developed by certified safety engineers
It prohibits them entirely, so AI cannot be used in any safety-related product sold in the EU market
It exempts them because existing functional safety standards already cover AI components
It classifies them as high-risk and imposes strict requirements on their development and testing

questions.explanation: The syllabus states that the EU AI Act classifies AI systems used as safety components as high-risk with strict development and testing requirements. Mature functional safety standards do not currently include AI, and the Act regulates rather than bans such components. Syllabus reference: CT-AI v2.0, section 2.1.2 (p. 23); AI-2.1.2 (K2).

questions.prompt: Which acceptance criterion is MOST appropriate for safety in an AI-based steering control system?

options.text: Non-AI components of the steering control system comply with ISO 26262-6 at the specified automotive safety integrity level
The steering control system ranks first on a public image-recognition benchmark against competing systems
The steering control system's dashboard follows the corporate design guide and uses accessible colours
The safety team retrains the steering model each night with the driving data collected that day

questions.explanation: The syllabus gives safety criteria such as compliance of non-AI components with ISO 26262-6 at a stated ASIL. Benchmark rankings do not address safety in the target context, interface design is usability, and nightly retraining is a process choice that could even weaken the safety argument. Syllabus reference: CT-AI v2.0, section 2.2.1 (p. 24); AI-2.2.1 (K2).

questions.prompt: What distinguishes supervised learning from unsupervised learning?

options.text: Supervised learning trains with a human watching the model; unsupervised learning trains automatically without any human involvement
Supervised learning trains on data in which each input has a corresponding output label; unsupervised learning infers structure without such labels
Supervised learning needs rewards and penalties from an environment; unsupervised learning needs an environment but no rewards
Supervised learning is used only for images; unsupervised learning is used only for text, audio and numerical sensor data

questions.explanation: Supervised learning uses labelled data to learn a mapping from inputs to outputs, while unsupervised learning finds patterns or structures in unlabelled data. 'Supervision' does not mean human observation, rewards define reinforcement learning, and neither form is restricted to one data type. Syllabus reference: CT-AI v2.0, section 3.1.1 (p. 27); AI-3.1.1 (K2).

questions.prompt: Which three activities of the ML workflow together form 'model generation'?

options.text: Prepare and test data, deploy the model and use the model
Understand the objectives, test the model and monitor the model
Select a framework, select the algorithm and test the model
Train the model, evaluate the model and tune the model

questions.explanation: The syllabus groups training, evaluation and tuning as 'model generation'; testing with an independent dataset follows once an acceptable model has been generated. The other lists combine activities from earlier or later stages of the workflow. Syllabus reference: CT-AI v2.0, section 3.1.2 (p. 28); AI-3.1.2 (K2).

questions.prompt: When a pretrained neural network is fine-tuned, which parts of the network can be trained further?

options.text: The entire network, specific layers (for example near the output end), or additional layers added to the network
The external document store alone, because fine-tuning adds knowledge without changing network layers
The input layer alone, because the hidden and output layers are fixed once a network has been pretrained on its data
The activation functions alone, because weights and biases cannot change after the network is pretrained

questions.explanation: The syllabus states that tuning can be applied to the entire network, to specific layers typically near the output end, or to additional layers. Adding knowledge without changing layers describes RAG, and fine-tuning adjusts weights and biases rather than being limited to inputs or activation functions. Syllabus reference: CT-AI v2.0, section 3.1.4 (p. 30); AI-3.1.4 (K2).

questions.prompt: What is the purpose of exploratory data analysis (EDA) performed alongside data preparation?

options.text: To gain insight into the data by discovering trends, patterns and anomalies and visualising the data with plots and charts
To generate the data labels automatically by clustering the data and naming each cluster after its centre
To explore the trained model's behavior by running unscripted test sessions against its user interface
To select the ML algorithm by trying every algorithm in the framework on the raw, uncleaned data

questions.explanation: EDA is carried out in parallel with data preparation to provide insights into the data, discovering trends, patterns and anomalies, and to visualise it with plots and charts. It is not exploratory testing of the model, automatic labelling or algorithm selection. Syllabus reference: CT-AI v2.0, section 3.2.1 (p. 31); AI-3.2.1 (K2).

questions.prompt: When suitable data is abundant, which factors typically determine how much data is used for training, evaluation and testing?

options.text: The expected model complexity, the algorithm used to train it, the available resources and the desired confidence in the model
The size of the user interface, the number of deployment targets, and the release date of the model
The number of testers, the colour depth of the images, and the order in which the data was collected
The licence of the ML framework, the number of stakeholders, and the length of the project's sprints

questions.explanation: The syllabus lists expected model complexity, the algorithm used, the availability of resources such as memory, disk space, computing power, bandwidth and time, and the desired confidence in the resultant model. The other lists are unrelated to dataset sizing. Syllabus reference: CT-AI v2.0, section 3.2.3 (p. 32); AI-3.2.3 (K2).

questions.prompt: A spam filter is tested on 200 emails, 50 of which are spam. It marks 40 emails as spam, and 30 of those really are spam. Which statement is correct?

options.text: Accuracy is 75.0% and F1 is 67.5
Accuracy is 85.0% and F1 is 67.5
Precision is 75.0% and recall is 60.0%
Precision is 60.0% and recall is 75.0%

questions.explanation: TP = 30, FP = 10, FN = 20, TN = 140. Precision = 30 / 40 = 75.0%; recall = 30 / 50 = 60.0%; accuracy = 170 / 200 = 85.0%; F1 = 2 × 75 × 60 / 135 = 66.7. Swapping precision and recall confuses the denominators, and 67.5 is the arithmetic mean rather than F1. Syllabus reference: CT-AI v2.0, section 3.3.1 (p. 33); AI-3.3.1 (K3).

questions.prompt: Which statement correctly describes the layers of a deep neural network?

options.text: The input layer stores the trained weights, hidden layers hold the training dataset, and the output layer contains the activation functions
The input layer receives data such as pixel values, hidden layers transform it into more abstract representations, and the output layer provides the result
The input layer and output layer are identical copies, and hidden layers exist only while the network is being trained in the cloud
The input layer produces the prediction, hidden layers receive raw sensor data, and the output layer calculates the loss during operation

questions.explanation: A DNN has an input layer that receives inputs, hidden layers of neurons that progressively transform the data, and an output layer that provides results such as the likelihood that an image shows a cat. The other options assign the wrong roles to the layers. Syllabus reference: CT-AI v2.0, section 3.4.1 (p. 36); AI-3.4.1 (K2).

questions.prompt: For k-multisection neuron coverage (kMNC) with k = 4, what is measured?

options.text: Four test inputs are generated per neuron, and kMNC is the proportion of inputs that were classified correctly
Four neurons are selected at random, and kMNC is the proportion of them whose output exceeds the threshold
Each layer is divided into four groups, and kMNC is the proportion of groups whose weights changed in training
Each neuron's possible output range is divided into four sections, and kMNC is the proportion of all sections activated during testing

questions.explanation: In kMNC the possible output range of each neuron is divided into k sections, and coverage is the proportion of these sections activated during testing. Random neuron selection, weight changes and classification accuracy are not part of the measure. Syllabus reference: CT-AI v2.0, section 3.4.3 (p. 37); AI-3.4.3 (K2).

questions.prompt: Why might a locked deep neural network still give slightly different outputs for the same input?

options.text: The network applies a reward function to each prediction, which reinforces different outputs for identical inputs
The network samples a new random training dataset for each prediction, which changes the decision boundary each time
The network keeps adjusting its weights after deployment, which makes it an adaptive system despite being described as locked
Floating-point precision limits and variations in hardware execution, such as parallel computation on GPUs, can cause non-deterministic behavior

questions.explanation: Although locked systems are generally considered deterministic, large neural networks can show non-deterministic behavior because of floating-point precision limits and hardware execution differences, especially with parallel computation or GPUs. A locked network does not keep learning, resample its training data or apply rewards in operation. Syllabus reference: CT-AI v2.0, section 4.1.1 (p. 39); AI-4.1.1 (K2).

questions.prompt: Why is a statistical approach especially important for AI-based systems in regulated industries such as healthcare and transport?

options.text: Regulators prohibit test data from operational environments, so statistical sampling must use synthetic data instead
Regulators require AI-based systems to be fully deterministic, which is shown by repeating one test case many times
Regulators often require evidence that safety or fairness thresholds are met with high confidence across a broad range of scenarios
Regulators accept statistical testing instead of any documentation, so statistical results remove the need for technical files and audits

questions.explanation: In regulated industries, demonstrating that an AI-based system meets safety or fairness thresholds with high confidence is often required, and statistical methods support claims across many scenarios rather than single examples. The other options invent regulatory rules not found in the syllabus. Syllabus reference: CT-AI v2.0, section 4.1.2 (p. 40); AI-4.1.2 (K2).

questions.prompt: What limitation does the CT-AI syllabus note about consulting domain experts to define expected results?

options.text: Experts can define expected results for locked systems, but not for adaptive systems that keep learning
Experts can help define expected results, but their opinions may differ and they can be wrong
Experts cannot define expected results until the model has been deployed to production
Experts must be certified under the EU AI Act before they can define expected results

questions.explanation: The syllabus states that domain experts can help define expected results, though their opinions might differ or be fallible. It does not restrict expert consultation to locked systems, require certification, or limit it to the period after deployment. Syllabus reference: CT-AI v2.0, section 4.1.3 (p. 40); AI-4.1.3 (K2).

questions.prompt: Which aspects does testing of GenAI outputs evaluate, according to the CT-AI syllabus?

options.text: Correctness, coherence and creativity, including originality and novelty, plus functional and non-functional requirements
The number of model parameters, the size of the training dataset and the cost of the GPU cluster
Code coverage of the transformer's source, cyclomatic complexity and adherence to naming conventions
Readability of the training logs, the speed of the CI pipeline and the number of open pull requests

questions.explanation: Testing GenAI involves evaluating the correctness, coherence and creativity of outputs, including originality and novelty, and verifying functional and non-functional requirements across text, images, video and audio. The other options describe code or project attributes rather than GenAI output quality. Syllabus reference: CT-AI v2.0, section 4.2.1 (p. 41); AI-4.2.1 (K2).

questions.prompt: During red teaming of a translation assistant, testers find that it translates dangerous weapon-building instructions when the request is framed as a story. What should the team do next according to the red-teaming approach?

options.text: Delete the conversation logs, because recording successful attacks would create a security risk for the assistant
Release the assistant unchanged, because story-framed requests are rare in normal translation usage
Switch to benchmark testing, because a successful attack shows that interactive prompting has finished its job
Analyse the failure to understand the threat, then create a dataset of such prompts to support mitigation and improve monitoring filters

questions.explanation: Red-teaming findings are analysed to understand the threats, and datasets created from them support mitigations and system improvements; insights also enhance blue-team monitoring and filters. Deleting evidence, ignoring the finding or abandoning interactive prompting would waste the result. Syllabus reference: CT-AI v2.0, section 4.2.2 (p. 42); AI-4.2.2 (K3).

questions.prompt: When AI is used as a service, what is the purpose of acceptance testing for that service?

options.text: To determine whether the service suits the intended system and whether, for example, the ML functional performance criteria are achieved
To confirm that the service's training data was split into training, validation and test sets in equal proportions
To retrain the service's model with the organisation's data so that the provider's results can be replaced
To verify that the service provider's source code follows the organisation's coding standards and naming conventions

questions.explanation: Where AI is used as a service, acceptance testing may be needed to determine the suitability of the service for the intended system and whether criteria such as ML functional performance have been achieved. Reviewing the provider's code, retraining the model or prescribing equal splits are not part of it. Syllabus reference: CT-AI v2.0, section 4.3.1 (p. 43); AI-4.3.1 (K2).

questions.prompt: Which list gives examples of test approaches specifically designed to address ML risks?

options.text: Boundary value analysis, state transition testing and decision table testing of the GUI
Data pipeline testing, adversarial testing and review of algorithm or model suitability
Usability testing, accessibility testing and localisation testing of the help pages
Unit testing, code review and static analysis of the login and billing modules

questions.explanation: The syllabus names data pipeline testing, adversarial testing and review of algorithm/model suitability as forms of testing designed for ML systems, covered in chapters 5 to 7. The other lists are conventional techniques applied to non-ML components. Syllabus reference: CT-AI v2.0, section 4.3.2 (p. 44); AI-4.3.2 (K2).

questions.prompt: Sensor readings used for training include temperatures of 900 °C from a room-temperature environment. Which mitigation fits this input data risk BEST?

options.text: Disparate impact analysis
Testing for overfitting and underfitting
Canary testing
Dataset constraint testing

questions.explanation: Out-of-range data, together with internally inconsistent datasets and wrong data types, is mitigated by dataset constraint testing. Disparate impact analysis targets bias, overfitting tests target the model, and canary testing targets deployment. Syllabus reference: CT-AI v2.0, section 5.1.1 (p. 47); AI-5.1.1 (K2).

questions.prompt: Which approach can detect bias without executing the model?

options.text: Running a known unbiased, representative dataset through the model and testing for outcome differences
Static analysis of data preparation programs and model code to find anti-patterns or mishandling of sensitive attributes
Feeding counterfactual loan applications through the model and comparing the approval rates for each group
Monitoring the deployed model's predictions for different age groups and comparing them over several weeks

questions.explanation: Static analysis of data preparation programs and model implementation code examines code without executing the model to find anti-patterns or mishandled sensitive attributes. The other approaches all execute the model and analyse its predictions. Syllabus reference: CT-AI v2.0, section 5.1.2 (p. 48); AI-5.1.2 (K2).

questions.prompt: What is the purpose of configuration management reviews in data pipeline testing?

options.text: To help verify that the correct pipeline code versions, settings and datasets are used in the training, test and production environments
To help verify that the model's predictions are explainable to regulators and that a model card has been published
To help verify that the pipeline runs faster than the previous version and that all data is stored in a public cloud
To help verify that the training dataset contains no outliers and that every label has been checked by an expert reviewer

questions.explanation: Configuration management reviews help verify that the correct pipeline code versions, configurations and datasets are used across training, testing and production. Outlier checks, explainability documentation and performance comparisons are other activities. Syllabus reference: CT-AI v2.0, section 5.1.3 (p. 49); AI-5.1.3 (K2).

questions.prompt: Which forms of misrepresentation does data representativeness testing address?

options.text: Skewed datasets, missing data, disproportionate feature distributions, inadequate coverage of operational scenarios and imbalanced classes
Values of the wrong type, duplicate records, out-of-range values and correlations that break defined rules
Slow pipeline throughput, insecure storage, uncontrolled code changes and failing installation scripts
Incorrect labels, inconsistent annotation guidelines, low inter-annotator agreement and ambiguous bounding boxes

questions.explanation: Data representativeness testing addresses skewed datasets, missing data, disproportionate feature distributions, inadequate coverage of operational scenarios and imbalanced class representation. Label problems belong to label correctness testing, rule violations to dataset constraint testing, and pipeline problems to data pipeline testing. Syllabus reference: CT-AI v2.0, section 5.1.4 (p. 50); AI-5.1.4 (K2).

questions.prompt: An employee dataset was extracted on 2026-09-30. One record has hire_date 2031-05-01. Which constraint would detect this defect, and at what scope does it apply?

options.text: A correlate constraint requiring hire dates to rise with salary, applied as a comparison constraint across records
A useful constraint requiring repeated hire dates, applied as a multi-value constraint across all employee records
A range constraint requiring hire_date on or before 2026-09-30, applied as a single-value constraint to each record
A duplicate constraint requiring unique hire dates, applied as a multi-value constraint across all employee records

questions.explanation: A hire date after the extraction date is out of range; a range constraint is a single-value constraint checked for each instance. Duplicate and useful constraints concern repetition across instances, and a correlation with salary is neither specified nor relevant to this defect. Syllabus reference: CT-AI v2.0, section 5.1.5 (p. 51); AI-5.1.5 (K3).

questions.prompt: Which combination of label correctness approaches does the syllabus describe as often most effective across a project?

options.text: Expert reviews early to establish clear guidelines, multiple annotation to refine labelling, and model-based checks as the model develops
Model-based checks before any labelling begins, expert reviews after deployment, and no multiple annotation at any stage
Multiple annotation of each data point by every annotator, with expert reviews and model-based checks omitted entirely
Automated rule-based tests alone, because human review introduces subjective errors into the labels of the dataset

questions.explanation: The syllabus suggests combining approaches: expert reviews to establish clear labelling guidelines early, inter-annotator agreement from multiple annotation to refine the labelling process, and model-based approaches to identify remaining label defects as the model develops. Syllabus reference: CT-AI v2.0, section 5.1.6 (p. 52); AI-5.1.6 (K2).

questions.prompt: Immediately after an updated model is deployed, the service fails to start. Which mitigation does the model risk table give for this risk?

options.text: Adversarial testing
Drift testing
Metamorphic testing
Smoke testing

questions.explanation: Deployment of an updated model that causes immediate failure is mitigated by smoke testing, while regression after deployment is mitigated by regression testing. Metamorphic, drift and adversarial testing address functional correctness, drift and robustness risks. Syllabus reference: CT-AI v2.0, section 6.1.1 (p. 55); AI-6.1.1 (K2).

questions.prompt: For a high-risk AI-based system, how does the syllabus describe the role of a documentation audit?

options.text: A documentation audit replaces functional testing for high-risk systems
Passing a documentation audit is often a prerequisite for deployment
A documentation audit is needed for systems that are not high-risk
A documentation audit is performed after the model has been retired

questions.explanation: The syllabus states that for high-risk systems, passing a documentation audit is often a prerequisite for deployment, while for all systems a thorough review helps verify quality. Audits do not replace testing and are not limited to non-high-risk or retired systems. Syllabus reference: CT-AI v2.0, section 6.1.2 (p. 56); AI-6.1.2 (K2).

questions.prompt: With a fixed margin of error, what happens to the confidence level of an accuracy estimate as more test cases are run?

options.text: It decreases, so the result becomes less certain
It becomes zero, because the error margin is fixed
It increases, so the result becomes more certain
It stays the same, because it depends on the model

questions.explanation: The syllabus describes two options as the number of tests increases: fix the confidence level and the margin of error decreases, or fix the margin of error and the confidence level increases, making the result more certain. The confidence level is not a property of the model alone. Syllabus reference: CT-AI v2.0, section 6.1.3 (p. 57); AI-6.1.3 (K2).

questions.prompt: Apart from building an equivalent model, which other black-box approach does the syllabus describe for adversarial testing?

options.text: A brute-force approach that runs a vast number of tests, hoping that some random inputs happen to cause misclassification
A back-to-back approach that compares the outputs of two models for identical inputs to find disagreements
A metamorphic approach that derives follow-up tests from source tests using a relation between their outputs
A white-box approach that analyses the model's parameters and training process to compute the adversarial perturbations directly

questions.explanation: Besides transferability from an equivalent model, the syllabus describes a brute-force approach that uses a vast number of tests in the hope that some coincide with adversarial examples. Analysing parameters is white-box, and metamorphic and back-to-back testing are different techniques. Syllabus reference: CT-AI v2.0, section 6.1.4 (p. 58); AI-6.1.4 (K2).

questions.prompt: A voice-recognition model transcribed a clear recording of 'turn on the kitchen lights' correctly. Which follow-up test case and expected result apply a valid metamorphic relation?

options.text: Reverse the recording so that it plays backwards and expect the same transcription
Add low-level background noise to the same recording and expect the same transcription
Add low-level background noise to the same recording and expect a clearly different transcription
Record a different sentence in the same voice and expect the same transcription

questions.explanation: A useful relation is invariance: a small perturbation such as low background noise should not change the transcription of the same utterance. A different sentence or a reversed recording changes the content, so the same output is not expected, and expecting a different transcription contradicts the invariance property. Syllabus reference: CT-AI v2.0, section 6.1.5 (p. 59); AI-6.1.5 (K3).

questions.prompt: A spam filter starts to miss new types of phishing emails that did not exist when it was trained. Which kind of drift does this describe?

options.text: Concept drift: the meaning of 'spam' has been redefined by new legislation for the same emails
Data drift: the statistical properties of operational input data have changed over time
Adversarial testing: the testers created the phishing emails as perturbations of legitimate ones
Underfitting: the model was too simple to learn the patterns in its original training data

questions.explanation: The syllabus uses a spam filter meeting new phishing attacks as an example of data drift, where operational input data becomes significantly different from training data. Concept drift would require the correct output for the same inputs to change, and the other options describe different problems. Syllabus reference: CT-AI v2.0, section 6.1.7 (p. 60); AI-6.1.7 (K2).

questions.prompt: Which situation can cause underfitting?

options.text: The model is too simple for the data, or the training data lacks features that reflect an important input-output relationship
The model learns the training data so well that it captures noise rather than the underlying pattern
The test dataset contains less common examples that were not used when the model was trained
The operational input data changes over time so that it differs from the training data distributions

questions.explanation: Underfitting occurs when a model is too simple to capture the structure of the data, or when the training data lacks features reflecting an important relationship. Learning noise is overfitting, changing input data is drift, and including less common examples is good practice when testing for overfitting. Syllabus reference: CT-AI v2.0, section 6.1.8 (p. 60); AI-6.1.8 (K2).

questions.prompt: An update to a smart-city transport routing system should reduce commuting times. How can A/B testing be applied, as in the syllabus example?

options.text: Compare the average journey duration for both variants on consecutive weeks, using agreed criteria and a statistical test
Compare the routing code of the two variants line by line to find defects where the implementations differ
Compare each route suggested by the new variant with a route calculated by hand by a traffic engineer
Compare the number of roads in the network before and after the update to confirm that coverage increased

questions.explanation: The syllabus example tests an update to a smart-city routing system by comparing average commute times for the two variants on consecutive weeks. A/B testing compares variants on agreed acceptance criteria with statistics, not by code review, manual expected results or network size. Syllabus reference: CT-AI v2.0, section 6.1.9 (p. 61); AI-6.1.9 (K2).

questions.prompt: In which situation does back-to-back testing provide significant value for an ML system?

options.text: When labelling a new training dataset, because back-to-back testing measures the inter-annotator agreement of the labels automatically
When choosing between two marketing offers, because back-to-back testing finds which offer customers prefer
When defining acceptance criteria, because back-to-back testing calculates the required margin of error
When migrating it to a new environment, such as from development to production, and comparing results across environments

questions.explanation: Back-to-back testing is valuable when migrating an MLS to a new environment, such as development to production, and when comparing results across environments; it can also reveal subtle defects in edge cases. Choosing between offers is A/B testing, and labelling or defining criteria are separate activities. Syllabus reference: CT-AI v2.0, section 6.1.10 (p. 62); AI-6.1.10 (K2).

questions.prompt: A developer calls a framework function with arguments in the wrong order, and training silently uses the wrong loss function. Which mitigation does the ML development risk table give for this risk?

options.text: Drift testing
API testing
Canary testing
Label correctness testing

questions.explanation: Incorrect or unintended use of library or framework APIs, for example in TensorFlow or PyTorch, is mitigated by API testing. Canary testing addresses deployment, drift testing addresses operational change, and label correctness testing addresses annotation. Syllabus reference: CT-AI v2.0, section 7.1.1 (p. 64); AI-7.1.1 (K2).

questions.prompt: What does API testing of a deployed machine learning system verify?

options.text: That it can be installed and uninstalled across supported environments, including dependencies such as GPU drivers and scripts
That it exposes well-defined, standards-compliant interfaces that handle inputs, outputs, error messages and integration with data feeds and clients
That it performs correctly across its intended deployment targets, from mobile and edge devices to cloud servers
That it keeps acceptable accuracy, behavior and efficiency after conversion from the training format to the deployment format

questions.explanation: API testing verifies well-defined, standards-compliant interfaces, correct handling of inputs and outputs and error messages, and integration with data feeds, clients and the pipeline. The other options describe installability, model conversion and cross-device testing. Syllabus reference: CT-AI v2.0, section 7.1.2 (p. 65); AI-7.1.2 (K2).
